ladder_notes: 21 rungs earned from 495 investor deals against 85,672 single-family homes, measured 2026-08-10. Window: 2026-01 .. 2026-06 (6 complete months).

Doors per deal and vs baseline are MARGINAL here: they price the next pull, not the list on its own. The Priority Ranking sheet scores every list standalone, which is why the same list carries different numbers on the two sheets. Both are right, they answer different questions.
Market share after is the running share of this county's investor deals your stack of pulls can reach. Total live doors is a same-day count of every home those pulls cover, counted once.

narrative: Every list on this page starts at a courthouse or a data provider. This one starts earlier: the owner has just passed, no probate case exists yet, and no provider list has the home. DataSift began recording obituary-linked homes in December 2025: 221 are flagged in Prince William County so far, about 28 new filings a month.

Of every 1,000 flagged homes, roughly 450 to 580 eventually sell, and investors buy 20 to 30 percent of those sales. Run that through the same doors-per-deal lens as the ranking sheet and obituary pencils out to 22 to 50 doors per deal (call it 34): about 4 to 6 times sharper than working random doors, behind only the sharpest court-record lists.

This is the model's base case, not this county's own sold history yet. The data only started in December 2025, so the earliest filings are just now reaching their selling window; as they age through it (early 2027) the number graduates to this county's real one.

timeline.what_happens: The owner passes. The flag turns on when the obituary publishes. No court record exists, no provider list has the home, and neither do your competitors.
The estate opens. Families typically file probate 30 to 90 days after the passing, once the funeral is behind them and an attorney is engaged.
The quiet stretch. Creditor windows (90 days in Florida, 4 months in Tennessee, similar elsewhere) and title work run their course. Very few of these homes close this early, and that is normal.

The first sales. Most states allow selling during administration, and heirs who need cash move first: as-is condition, documented 5 to 7 percent discounts, often off-market. Roughly a quarter of these homes sell inside the first year.
The main wave. A typical administration settles around month 14, and the sales concentrate here. This is the window the whole cadence builds toward.
The tail, then the keepers. About half of these homes have sold by year three. The rest stay in the family, and once a home transfers to heirs who keep it, the sale signal fades fast.

ftm.office_address: 4379 Ridgewood Center Dr, Prince William, VA 22192
ftm.notes: The Tax Administration's Collections staff is responsible for collecting past due taxes. While a direct 'delinquent roll' for public download isn't explicitly stated, the office manages these accounts. Contacting the office directly or monitoring the tax sale auction list (which is derived from this roll) is the best approach. Payment plans are offered to delinquent taxpayers.

ftm.office_official: City of Manassas Treasurer / City of Manassas Park Treasurer
ftm.office_address: Manassas: 9025 Center St, Manassas, VA 20110 / Manassas Park: 103 Manassas Park Dr, Manassas Park, VA 20111
ftm.notes: Prince William County has two incorporated cities: Manassas and Manassas Park, which levy their own property taxes. Separate research is required for their delinquent tax rolls. Check their respective Treasurer's offices for information on delinquent properties and potential tax sales.

Virginia has no separate probate court; the Clerk of Circuit Court handles probate. To schedule an appointment, a pre-appointment worksheet must be completed. Records are indexed by decedent name, not property address. A separate assessor lookup is needed to link to property.

ftm.data_type: Foreclosure (first public signal for this state's process)
ftm.office_official: Circuit Court Clerk's Office - Land Records
ftm.notes: Virginia is a non-judicial foreclosure state. The first public signal is a recorded Notice of Default or Trustee Sale. These are filed with the Circuit Court Clerk's Land Records division. Online access to Land Records Management System (LRMS) is available via subscription. Deeds prior to 1918 are not available online.

ftm.data_type: Recorder / Register of Deeds - Lien & Deed Index
ftm.office_official: Circuit Court Clerk's Office - Land Records
ftm.notes: The Clerk's Office maintains deeds and related land records (indexes and images from 1918 to present). Mechanic's, IRS & state tax, HOA, child-support liens, and lis pendens are indexed here. Online access is available via subscription to the Land Records Management System (LRMS). Tax and child-support liens are indexed against the person, requiring a name-match to the assessor roll.

ftm.office_official: County Attorney's Office / TACS (Taxing Authority Consulting Services)
ftm.office_address: 1 County Complex Ct, Prince William, VA 22192 (County Attorney)
ftm.notes: Virginia is a tax deed state. The County Attorney's Office provides a list of tax foreclosure auction properties. Auctions are facilitated by third-party contractors like TACS. Lists are published as legal notices weeks before the sale. It is crucial to market the owner before the auction. Sign-up for email notifications of upcoming sales is available through TACS.

ftm.office_official: City of Manassas - Code Enforcement / City of Manassas Park - Code Enforcement
ftm.office_address: Manassas: 9025 Center St, Manassas, VA 20110 / Manassas Park: 103 Manassas Park Dr, Manassas Park, VA 20111
ftm.notes: Code violations are typically a city function. Both Manassas and Manassas Park have dedicated Code Enforcement divisions. Check their websites for online portals or contact information for records requests. Accela 'Citizen Access' portals are common for cities, allowing for online searches and potentially data exports.

ftm.office_address: 5 County Complex Ct, Prince William, VA 22192
ftm.notes: The County's Code Enforcement division handles violations in unincorporated areas. They have an online portal for reporting violations and checking status. Records requests for specific properties may be necessary for detailed information. Online indexes for code violations are often less robust than city-level systems.

ftm.office_official: Prince William County - Building Development Division (Code Enforcement)
ftm.office_address: 5 County Complex Ct, Prince William, VA 22192
ftm.notes: Information regarding condemned or unsafe structures and demolition orders would typically fall under the purview of Code Enforcement or the Building Development Division. While a specific 'condemned list' isn't explicitly advertised, these records would be part of their enforcement actions. A public records request may be required to obtain a list of such properties.

ftm.office_official: Prince William County General District Court Clerk
ftm.notes: Eviction (Unlawful Detainer) dockets are maintained by the General District Court. Online access to court records may be available through the Virginia Judicial System's online portal (case information system). Searching for multiple filings by the same plaintiff (landlord) would be the method to identify 'multiple-eviction landlords'. This often requires manual review or specialized data access.

ftm_narrative: Data gaps to know about: SiftMap data (provider data) is low or zero in Prince William County, VA for: Foreclosure notices, Tax sale list. These are proven deal-makers nationally, and nobody can buy them here, so the county pulls below are not a backup, they are the only way in: treat them as priority pulls. Also not in SiftMap here: Eviction filings, Code violations, Divorce filings.
Sources pulled straight from the county the day records publish, 30 to 90 days before paid data. 'Verify locally' means confirm the link before you work it.

read_me.Doors/deal: How many homes you have to work to find one deal. A smaller number is better.
read_me.Vs baseline: How many times better this list is than mailing every home in the county. 5x means five times better.
read_me.Deals (6mo): How many homes from this list an investor bought in the last 6 months.
read_me.Deal Share %: Out of all the deals in this county, how many came from this list.
read_me.List Size: How many homes are on this list right now.
read_me.Typical gross: The profit built into a typical deal here: what the home is worth minus what it sold for.
read_me.Priority: Work the Priority 1 rows first. They find deals the fastest. Then Priority 2. Priority 3 is extra.
read_me.Signal: The list of homes this row is about.
read_me.Type: List = homes on one list. Stack = homes on two lists at once. AI score = homes the computer score picked.
read_me.Rung: The order to pull in. Rung 1 is the best value in the county, then work down.
read_me.New deals reached: Deals this rung unlocks that the rungs above it did not already cover.
read_me.Market share after %: Out of all this county's investor deals, the share your stack of pulls can now reach.
read_me.Total live doors: Every live door you are marketing to after pulling this rung and everything above it, each home counted once.
read_me.Which tabs you get: One tab per section the page is showing for this county, in the same order. Sections the page hides for this county are not exported, so the file and the screen always carry the same set.
read_me.Work Order: The ranking tab for counties the site shows a ladder for. It is a pull order: each rung counts only the deals the rungs above have not already given you, so doors per deal is what that pull costs you NEXT, not what the list is worth on its own.
read_me.Priority Ranking: The ranking tab you get instead when a county has no ladder. Every list is scored standalone against the county baseline. The website makes the same swap, so this workbook only ever carries one ranking, the one on screen.
read_me.Rating (1-5): The ZIP leaderboard's star rating, written as a number. Five stars is the strongest ZIP in this county's own closed deals.
read_me.Momentum (x): Recent deal pace against this ZIP's own earlier pace. Above 1.5x reads as heating up, at or below 0.75x as cooling.
read_me.best odds: On Price Bands, the value band where a deal takes the fewest doors worked, among bands with enough supply and enough deals to trust.
read_me.Non-disclosure states: Sale prices are not public there, so deal-dollar columns are omitted; doors per deal and lift never use dollars.
read_me.Evidence A / B / C: from this county's own sold deals / cross-market benchmark / single-market anchor (Knox + Blount TN AI measurement)
read_me.Verify supply: The row tripped the verify rule (v2.1 coverage-aware: verify reasons annotate (churn: doors/deal < 5; small: list < 250) without demoting; only judicial notice lists and churn artifacts (doors/deal < 1) force P3. Volume floors: P1 needs >=2% of county deal flow or >=25 deals, P2 >=1% or >=12 deals): demand is real, treat the efficiency as directional until you price the live list.
read_me.The window: Every count here is the rolling six months the site is showing. Deal counts are read fresh, because county recorders keep filing deeds for weeks after a window closes.
